notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Keep the booking, the account and the next action in agreement.
intro: A proposed integration-quality workbench for Wealth.com, connecting advisory-firm identity, booking events and reviewed CRM updates.
queueIntro: Fictional advisory organizations and business events only. No client estate documents, tax records, assets or personal financial details are included.
workbenchIntro: Inspect a proposed revenue-system update before it propagates. This demo uses local review receipts and never writes to Salesforce or another GTM platform.
firstBody: Resolve the advisory organization, check the current booking and opportunity state, and attach the event key and recovery owner to the proposed action.

fields.label: Required CRM fields and update owners validated
AI-generated summary is tied to business evidence
Failure handling and receiving owner assigned

rules.title: Resolve the advisory organization
rules.next: Distinguish an advisor, branch and parent firm before assigning an enterprise account.

rules.title: Make the event replay-safe
rules.next: Record a stable event key so a repeated booking or CRM event does not create another task.

rules.title: Reconcile the lifecycle state
rules.next: A canceled meeting, active opportunity and new inquiry require different actions. Refresh the authoritative state.

rules.title: Validate the proposed field changes
rules.next: Check required values and field ownership before preparing a CRM update.

rules.title: Review the generated summary
rules.next: Keep the summary grounded in the business conversation. Do not add client estate, tax or financial details.

rules.title: Assign recovery and follow-up
rules.next: A failed sync needs an owner and a replay plan, while a completed handoff needs a receiving seller.

ready.title: Ready for a revenue-integration review
ready.next: The reviewer can inspect the account, event and proposed fields. A repeated event should reuse its decision key rather than create another task.

experiments.name: Current-state booking handoff
experiments.hypothesis: Checking authoritative state reduces incorrect follow-up tasks.
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Evidence-backed business summaries
experiments.guardrail: Unsupported claims and sensitive client details
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Map the integration layer
roadmap.body: Work with the Director of RevOps on systems, source-of-truth fields, event keys and failure ownership.
roadmap.measure: Documented flows and known data breaks

roadmap.title: Ship one tested automation
roadmap.body: Pilot booking-to-CRM proposals with current-state checks, replay protection and visible recovery.

roadmap.title: Measure reliability and team effort
roadmap.body: Instrument failures and reviewer corrections. Document maintenance and compare before-and-after effort for the same task.
roadmap.measure: Recoverable failures, accepted output and measured effort

metricsTitle: A delivered event is not necessarily a correct handoff.
metricsIntro: Synthetic integration scorecard distinguishes delivery, validation and useful output.
metricsNotes: Counts are invented and do not describe Wealth.com’s production systems.
The 43 accepted, six conflicted and three invalid events reconcile to 52 unique events.
This is revenue operations, not estate, tax or investment advice.
